discovery: Discovery of superconductivity in organic molecular conductors (the Bechgaard salts)

nominees.name: Denis Jérome
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Solides, CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, Orsay, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons in organic conductors
motivation: In 1980 Jérome, using high-pressure transport, found superconductivity in (TMTSF)2PF6, a crystal synthesised by Bechgaard. This was the first organic superconductor, and it confirmed a decades-old prediction that molecular solids could carry electrons without resistance. The Bechgaard salts and the BEDT-TTF families that followed became a uniquely tunable laboratory for many-body physics. Modest pressure can move them through spin-density waves, field-induced quantized Hall phases, unconventional superconductivity next to antiferromagnetism, bandwidth-controlled Mott transitions and quantum spin liquids. These materials showed that low dimensionality and strong correlation, not the chemistry of any particular atom, decide a material's ground state. That insight anticipated much of the later work on cuprates and other unconventional superconductors. Their discovery joined synthetic chemistry and condensed-matter physics in a collaboration that remains a model for the field. It created a whole discipline that still yields new quantum phases after four decades.
